newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian bridegroom in trouble over dowry demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian bridegroom in trouble over dowry demand.

text.p: A young Indian computer engineer is in trouble after he miscalculated a bid to extract more dowry money from his father-in-law, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Tuesday.
PTI said the High Court in India's eastern state of Orissa ordered a probe into the December 13 affair after a newspaper reported it.
According to the report the bridegroom was paid 50,000 rupees ($1,400) as the dowry he had initially demanded from his father-in-law.
But on the wedding day he demanded a further 150,000 rupees ($4,200) as a condition for going through with the Hindu marriage ritual.
The unidentified father-in-law hastily borrowed the money from friends so the wedding would go ahead.
Demanding or giving dowry is a criminal offence in India, where every year hundreds of women are reported burned to death after being doused with kerosene. The killings are called "dowry deaths".
Women activists say many more deaths go unreported because of the stigma attached to failed marriages.
